quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results: revenue $29 million, up 13% year over year and 7% sequentially. Licensing and related revenue rose 21% to $18.2 million (63% of revenue), the strongest licensing quarter in three years; royalty revenue $10.8 million (37%), versus $10.7 million a year earlier and up 17% sequentially on wireless connectivity, automotive AI and smartphone share gains. 10 licensing agreements signed, including two with first-time customers and two directly with OEMs. Gross margin 87% GAAP / 88% non-GAAP; non-GAAP operating income $3.1 million versus $0.8 million, margin 11% versus 3%; GAAP net loss $2.9 million; non-GAAP net income up 28% to $2.3 million. About $221 million in cash and deposits; 406 employees including 327 engineers.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $29 million (+13% YoY); licensing $18.2 million (+21%); royalties $10.8 million (+17% QoQ); non-GAAP operating margin 11%

quarterly_data.signal: Shipments of CEVA-powered devices in Q2: 567 million, up 16% year over year. Mobile handset modems 61 million units (11% of the total) versus 55 million; consumer IoT 487 million versus 409 million; industrial IoT 19 million versus 24 million, though industrial royalty revenue rose 7% on a richer mix including automotive AI and wireless infrastructure. By technology: Bluetooth 295 million, down 16%; Cellular IoT a record 68 million, up 3%; Wi-Fi 80 million, up 28%.
quarterly_data.figure: 567 million devices (+16%); handset modems 61 million; Bluetooth 295 million (-16%); Cellular IoT 68 million (+3%); Wi-Fi 80 million (+28%)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised: 2026 revenue now expected to grow 13% to 15% over 2025 (previously 12%); total costs still up approximately 8%; non-GAAP operating income now expected up approximately 70% and non-GAAP net income up approximately 50%. The second half is expected to be stronger than the first, while 'memory pricing dynamics and broader supply constraints remain important industry variables'. Q3 2026: revenue $30.5 million to $34.5 million; gross margin approximately 87% GAAP / 88% non-GAAP; non-GAAP operating expenses $22.5 million to $23.5 million. CFO: in each of the last three years second-half volume rose north of 30% year over year, and new automotive royalty payers started earlier this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue +13% to 15% (from 12%); non-GAAP operating income +~70%; Q3 revenue $30.5 million to $34.5 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: a leading global AI and computing platform company (unnamed; it develops both the hardware platform and the operating system) selected CEVA's NeuPro-M NPU IP for its next-generation custom AI silicon — 'one of the most strategically significant AI licensing agreements in CEVA's history' and a new category of AI customer. The custom engagement drives significantly higher royalty per unit than the standard NPU offering; such engagements typically reach tape-out within a few quarters, then about one and a half to two years to production. CEO sees GlobalFoundries' acquisition of ARC as a tailwind for NeuPro NPU licensing in the U.S. and the Western world. CFO: AI is about 20% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: one and a half to two years from tape-out to production; AI about 20% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Platform wins. A high-volume U.S. semiconductor company adopted one complete chip built on CEVA's Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth Low Energy IP rather than licensing the IP blocks individually; another U.S. customer expanded from a single baseband component to CEVA's complete baseband processing subsystem (full MAC and baseband hardware and software, excluding RF). CEO: complete-platform deals carry meaningfully higher licensing and future royalty than component IP, increase stickiness and tilt make-versus-buy toward CEVA. CEVA also launched Microsoft-certified RealSpace Elevate spatial-audio software, entering PC gaming. CFO: licensing and related revenue ran at roughly $18 million a quarter in the first half versus $15-$16 million a year earlier, and he believes these levels can continue.
quarterly_data.figure: licensing run rate ~$18 million per quarter vs $15-$16 million a year earlier

quarterly_data.signal: Customer UNISOC. CFO: UNISOC, CEVA's Chinese customer in low-cost smartphones, is moving more to 5G (higher ASPs for CEVA) and has won a few dozen design wins with Chinese brands including Vivo and Xiaomi, which previously used MediaTek more extensively. CEO: entry-level handset royalties recovered meaningfully from Q1 to Q2 as these customers gain share; CEVA also expects share gains in the second half with its U.S. customers as they use more of their internal modem.

Memory shortage. CFO: low-end smartphones need much less memory than high-end devices, so CEVA has not seen significant issues in the last couple of quarters; the constraint hurts margins in the supply chain and bites more at the $1,000-phone end. CEO: 'the memory shortage has an impact on the wireless handset industry, and it's hard to quantify exactly how that will impact the second half'; the mobile outlook assumes typical seasonality with the caveat of memory allocation challenges.

Bluetooth HDT: CEO says HDT carries a higher royalty per unit than legacy Bluetooth, further raised when paired with CEVA's RF IP; volume ramp starts toward the end of this year with a significant ramp through 2027 and 2028, and the announced customer is ramping the product now. CEO expects Wi-Fi shipments to keep healthy year-over-year growth, with some high-volume ramps starting in Q3 and Q4. Edge-AI opportunities he cites: PC and mobile, automotive ADAS, and robotics and humanoids starting now.
